defects.description: The divmod arguments are swapped: `divmod(arabic, number)` divides the table value by the running number, but it must divide the number by the value (`divmod(number, arabic)`).
paraphrases: `divmod(arabic, number)` has its operands reversed; conversion needs `divmod(number, arabic)`.
The quotient/remainder are computed from (value, number) instead of (number, value).
Argument-order bug: the number should be divided by each Roman value, not the reverse.
defects.rationale: Upstream is `divmod(number, arabic)`. Real (wrong factors and remainder), findable against the conversion logic and the docstring, distinct.

defects.description: Each symbol is repeated `factor + 1` times instead of `factor`, appending one extra copy of every Roman symbol.
paraphrases: `roman * (factor + 1)` should be `roman * factor`; it adds an extra symbol each step.
The repetition count is off by one, so e.g. a factor of 3 emits four symbols.
One too many copies of each numeral are appended.
defects.rationale: Upstream is `roman * factor`. Real (extra symbols), findable against the docstring (int_to_roman(3) == 'III'), distinct.

defects.description: The loop breaks when the remaining number is non-zero (`if number != 0`), so it stops after the first iteration; it should break once the number has been fully converted (`if number == 0`).
paraphrases: `if number != 0` is inverted; the loop should terminate when `number == 0`.
The break condition stops the conversion prematurely, as soon as any remainder remains.
Termination logic is backwards: it exits while there is still work left to do.
defects.rationale: Upstream is `if number == 0:`. Real (premature termination), findable from the loop's intent and the docstring, distinct from the other defects.
